core_obligations: Induction set-up (proof lines 748-750): fix a in A; assume f and g already agree below a; aim f(a) = g(a).
Down-set comparison (lines 751-757): if x lessdot f(a) then f-inverse(x) < a, so the hypothesis transports x below g(a); the converse direction is symmetric.
Finish (lines 758-762): the two down-sets agree, extensionality for strict linear orders gives f(a) = g(a), and well-ordering induction propagates this to all of A.
proof_roadmap: Induct on a in A via well-ordering induction.
Under the induction hypothesis, compare the strict lower sets of f(a) and g(a) elementwise.
Identify the two lower sets and conclude f(a) = g(a) by the named extensionality fact.
Close the induction to get f = g everywhere.
